summary: @next-fonts/font typosquat executes attacker-controlled code fetched from blockchain endpoints
details: Package name and API (`Inter()` returning `{style, className}`) mimic @next/font to lure Next.js developers. When `Inter()` is called, the package decodes a base64-hidden payload via `atob(...)`, spawns it in a detached child process with `spawn('node', ['-e', code], {detached:true, stdio:'ignore'})`, and falls back to `eval(code)` on spawn error. The decoded payload fetches an encrypted command string from a Tron account via api.trongrid.io, with fallbacks to fullnode.mainnet.aptoslabs.com, bsc-dataseed.binance.org, and bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, XOR-decrypts it with hardcoded keys, and passes the result to `eval`. Using on-chain data as the C2 channel allows the attacker to update the executed payload without changing the package and evades URL blocklists. Any Next.js application that imports this package and invokes `Inter()` will execute arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the developer or build host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
